subject: Post-call: Packly inference workload snapshot & scaling asks
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina@packly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Packly inference workload snapshot & scaling asks

Nina — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a tight scope for sizing and pilot: 

- High-level workload: user-facing summarization + follow-up clarification in a streaming websocket flow (partial tokens sent as they are generated).
- Latency targets: p95 target ~300ms (acceptable range 250–350ms) for interactive sessions; p99 is less critical but should not exceed 1.2s in normal conditions.
- Steady-state expectations: ~60 QPS average (in prod after ramp).
- Burst profile: short bursts up to ~900 QPS lasting 30–90s (observed during marketing peaks).
- Typical tokens per request (input+output): ~320 tokens (your estimate).
- Streaming concurrency: 8–12 simultaneous active streams that need partial-output latency guarantees.
- Batch/async: offline embedding jobs (not in scope for interactive SLO).

What we need from you to proceed:
1) A short workload snapshot (CSV or JSONL) with sample timestamps, request size, and a few payloads — attached is a one-row example I prepared (packly_workload_snapshot.csv).
2) Confirmation on peak burst duration and whether bursts are regional or global.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll produce an initial sizing estimate and a recommended config for a dedicated pilot (GPU class, model variant, batching & streaming settings).
- Can we book a 60-min profiling session (we’ll run a short test harness against your sandbox) next week?

Attaching: packly_workload_snapshot.csv (example row).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Dylan on sizing.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Packly inference workload snapshot & scaling asks

Tessa — quick ops read on the numbers above. High-level notes for sizing team: 

- If avg tokens/request ~320 and steady QPS ~60, sustained tokens/sec ~19.2k. That’s small in absolute tokens but streaming and p95 latency constraints push us toward lower-batch, low-queue configurations.
- Burst to 900 QPS for 30–90s implies a very high short-term concurrency need. We should assume the customer will want headroom ~1.5x to 2x above observed peaks for safety.
- Streaming specifics: websocket partial outputs require per-request KV-cache hits and minimal compilation warmup. We should recommend a model variant that supports fast generation on short sequences (e.g., quantized 4-bit Llama2-13B variant we validated for streaming).

Actionables I’ll prepare:
- initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx: rough instance-counts for pilot (ephemeral dedicated nodes), cost ballpark, and a latency/throughput tradeoff table.
- checklist for profiling session (tokenization parity, sample payload file: payload_samples.jsonl).

Two quick questions for Tessa/Nina: 1) Are the bursts global (all regions) or limited to US-EAST? 2) Do you expect large variance in output length (e.g., sometimes 800+ output tokens)?

— Marissa (platform sizing)

Attachment: initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx (stub)
From: Nina Patel <nina@packly.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@packly.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Packly inference workload snapshot & scaling asks

Thanks, Tessa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed avg tokens/request: 320 (input ~120, average generated ~200). Occasionally some long-form outputs hit ~700 tokens but that’s <1% of requests.
- Steady-state: 60 QPS predominantly US regions (US-EAST primary, small tail in EU).
- Burst behavior: Global campaigns sometimes hit ~900 QPS across regions, but each region sees staggered spikes — US-EAST is the dominant contributor. Burst windows are typically 30–45s.
- Streaming: Yes — websockets that require early-token delivery (clients render partial output). We care about p95 for partial token arrival and overall response completion.

We’ll attach a small payload_samples.jsonl (sanitized) and a 24-hr sample of request counts. We’d like a cost ballpark and model suggestions prior to the profiling call.

Would Tue/Wed next week work for the profiling session?

— Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Platform | Packly
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina@packly.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Packly inference workload snapshot & scaling asks

Nina — thanks for the clarifications. Quick technical mapping and ask list before we run profiling: 

- SLO mapping: we’ll treat the streaming p95 requirement as two checks: partial-token p95 <= 300ms and final-response p95 <= 350ms. Both are achievable with a dedicated pilot and tuned batching (low-latency mode).
- Throughput plan: pilot config we propose: 3 dedicated GPU nodes (A100 / equivalent) with optimized kernels and small batch windows to keep latency low; autoscale/burst policy to add 2 extra nodes for burst windows. This is an initial estimate — Marissa will share the workbook.
- Concurrency: we’ll instrument websocket sessions to measure per-connection KV-cache hits; for profiling, we need a sample of 20 concurrent streams at realistic pacing to validate per-connection memory.

Can you share the sanitized payload_samples.jsonl and confirm a profiling window of 20 minutes where Packly can accept test traffic? We’ll provide a short harness and one-time credentials for the sandbox.

Link to profiling plan (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/packly/workload-signature

— Dylan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps and owners so we don’t lose momentum: 

1) Packly (Nina / ops) — upload sanitized payload_samples.jsonl and a 24-hr request-count CSV to the Drive folder by Fri 2027-05-13.
2) Redwood (Marissa/Dylan) — deliver an initial sizing estimate (workbook attached) and model variant recommendations by Mon 2027-05-14.
3) Profiling session — target week of 2027-05-17. Nina, can you confirm Tue/Wed availability? We’ll reserve a 60-min slot and provide the test harness and temporary sandbox keys.
4) Commercials check — I’ll send a brief note on pilot duration and pricing bands once we validate the profile.

Attachments (in this thread): packly_workload_snapshot.csv, initial_sizing_estimate.xlsx, payload_samples.jsonl

If anyone needs an earlier turn on the sizing workbook, flag here and Connor will prioritize.

— Tessa
